{{nihongo|'''Yamashina Shrine'''|山科神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamashiro Province]].

It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}), and under the former {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=shrine ranking system}} it was a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
The current enshrined deities are the following two<ref name="board">Explanatory board in the precincts.</ref>.
:* {{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto}} (やまとたけるのみこと)
:* Wakatake-no-Ō (わかたけのみこと) - son of Yamato Takeru.
In the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, the number of enshrined seats is recorded as two.

=== History ===
=== Overview ===
Shrine tradition says it was founded by imperial command of {{ill|Emperor Uda|Q349267|qid=Q349267}} in {{ill|Kanpyō (era)|de|Kanpyō|fa|کانپیو (دوره)|fr|Ère Kanpyō|hr|Kanpyō (razdoblje)|ia|Kanpyo|id|Kampyō|ja|寛平|ko|간표|ru|Кампё|sh|Kanpyō (era)|simple|Kanpyō (era)|sr|Канпјо (ера)|tr|Kanpyō|uk|Кампьо (ненґо)|zh|寬平|zh_yue|寬平|qid=Q1346292}} 9 ({{ill|897|ab|897|af|897|als|897|am|897 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|897|ar|897|ary|897|ast|897|avk|897|az|897|azb|۸۹۷ (میلادی)|bar|897|bcl|897|be|897|be_x_old|897|bg|897|bn|৮৯৭|bpy|মারি ৮৯৭|br|897|bs|897.|ca|897|cdo|897 nièng|ceb|897|ckb|٨٩٧|crh|897|cs|897|csb|897|cv|897|cy|897|da|897|de|897|el|897|eml|897|eo|897|es|897|et|897|eu|897|fa|۸۹۷ (میلادی)|fi|897|fo|897|fr|897|fy|897|ga|897|gan|897年|gd|897|gl|897|he|897|hi|897|hr|897.|ht|897 (almanak jilyen)|hu|897|hy|897|id|897|ilo|897|io|897|is|897|it|897|ja|897年|jv|897|ka|897|kaa|897|kk|897 жыл|ko|897년|la|897|lb|897|lij|897|lmo|897|lt|897 m.|lv|897. gads|map_bms|897|mdf|897|mg|897|mhr|897|mi|897|mk|897|mr|इ.स. ८९७|mrj|897 и|ms|897|mzn|۸۹۷|nah|897|nap|897|nds|897|new|सन् ८९७|nl|897|nn|897|no|897|nrm|897|nso|897|oc|897|or|୮୯୭|os|897-æм аз|pl|897|pnb|897|pt|897|qu|897|ro|897|ru|897 год|rue|897|sa|८९७|scn|897|sd|897ع|se|897|sh|897.|shn|897|si|897|sk|897|sl|897|smn|897|sq|897|sr|897|su|897|sv|897|sw|897|tg|Соли 897|th|พ.ศ. 1440|tk|897|tl|897|tly|897|tr|897|tt|897 ел|uk|897|ur|897ء|uz|897|vec|897|vi|897|war|897|wuu|897年|xmf|897|zh|897年|zh_min_nan|897 nî|zh_yue|897年|qid=Q30468}})<ref name="board"/>. It is said to have been the ancestral deity of the local powerful Miyamichi clan<ref name="board"/>.

In the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} compiled in {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Engi}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), under {{ill|Uji district|fr|District d'Uji|ja|宇治郡|ko|우지군|zh|宇治郡|qid=Q10946235}}, {{ill|Yamashiro Province|cs|Provincie Jamaširo|de|Provinz Yamashiro|es|Provincia de Yamashiro|fa|ولایت یاماشیرو|fr|Province de Yamashiro|gl|Provincia de Yamashiro|hak|Yamashiro-koet|id|Provinsi Yamashiro|it|Yamashiro (provincia)|ja|山城国|ko|야마시로국|lt|Jamaširo žemė|ms|Yamashiro Province|nl|Yamashiro (provincie)|pt|Província de Yamashiro|ru|Ямасиро (провинция)|simple|Yamashiro Province|sk|Jamaširo (provincia)|sr|Провинција Јамаширо|tr|Yamashiro (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ямашіро|wuu|山城国|zh|山城國|zh_min_nan|Yamasiro-kok|zh_yue|山城國|qid=Q749276}}, it is listed as "two seats of Yamashina Shrine, both Myojin major, receiving offerings at monthly and niiname rites," indicating both seats ranked as {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}} and received court offerings for {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11516161}} and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|de|Niiname-sai|fr|Niiname-no-Matsuri|id|Niiname-no-Matsuri|ja|新嘗祭|ko|신상제 (11월)|simple|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518}}{{Sfn|Yamashina Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. Also, in ''{{ill|Fusō Ryakuki|Q11076282|qid=Q11076282}}''<ref group="原" name="Engi6"/>, it is recorded that in {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Engi}} 6 ({{ill|928|Q24297|qid=Q24297}}), "Yamashina Ōkami" was promoted to Senior Fourth Rank, Lower{{Sfn|Yamashina Festival (Kokushi Daijiten)}}{{Sfn|Yamashina Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}.

Documents also attest to the shrine festival "'''Yamashina Festival'''". ''{{ill|Honchō Gatsuryō|Q11520401|qid=Q11520401}}''<ref group="原">''Honchō Gatsuryō'', upper third month, Yamashina festival entry.</ref> states that in Kanpyō 10 ({{ill|898|Q24131|qid=Q24131}}) the festival became an official court festival{{Sfn|Yamashina Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. The {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Engishiki}}<ref group="原">''Engishiki'' vol.15 (Kuraryō), Yamashina Festival entry.</ref> records that it was held annually on the day of the first snake of the 4th and 11th months. Since {{ill|Fujiwara no Taneko|Q11623488|qid=Q11623488}}, born to Miyamichi no Retsuko (daughter of {{ill|Miyaji no Iyamasu|Q65262147|qid=Q65262147}}) and {{ill|Fujiwara no Takafuji|Q5507544|qid=Q5507544}}, became the birth mother of {{ill|Emperor Daigo|Q329753|qid=Q329753}} (reigned from Kanpyō 9 [897] to Engi 8 [930]), it has been pointed out that the Miyamichi clan's position as the emperor's maternal relatives was the background for official designation of the Yamashina Festival{{Sfn|Yamashina Festival (Kokushi Daijiten)}}.

However, the "Yamashina deity" in these sources is also theorized to refer instead to {{ill|Iwaya Shrine|Q11049290|qid=Q11049290|lt=Iwaya Shrine}} (Ōyake Nakakōji-chō, Yamashina Ward) or Miyamichi Shrine (Kanjūji Niōdō-chō, Yamashina Ward), and the matter is not settled{{Sfn|Yamashina Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. Iwaya Shrine is said to have been this shrine's inner shrine (now independent), and when {{ill|Ōishi Yoshio|Q530128|qid=Q530128}} lived in concealment in Yamashina, he is said to have secluded himself at Iwaya Shrine to pray for fulfillment of his great aim<ref name="board"/>.

In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it was called "Nishi-Iwaya Daimyōjin" or "Ichinomiya"<ref name="KyotoCity"/>.

After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, the shrine was renamed to the present "Yamashina Shrine"{{Sfn|Yamashina Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. In {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} 6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}), it was ranked as a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}} in the modern shrine ranking system{{Sfn|Yamashina Festival (Kokushi Daijiten)}}.
